title: Monitoring and Production Maintenance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Monitoring and Production Maintenance in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Monitoring and Production Maintenance within Server-Side Rendering, Nuxt, and Deployment. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Rendering choices affect initial content, hydration, deployment complexity, caching, security, and the availability of browser-only APIs.

content_blocks.title: Monitoring and Production Maintenance: Measure before optimizing
content_blocks.alt_text: Measure before optimizing diagram for lesson 145: Monitoring and Production Maintenance. Record the same route, data, and device → Identify the actual render or bundle bottleneck → Repeat measurements and check behavior
content_blocks.caption: Performance workflow: measure a reproducible baseline, optimize the observed bottleneck, and repeat the same test.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue rendering may be client-side, server-rendered, or pre-rendered; Nuxt provides an opinionated application framework for SSR/SSG use cases. This lesson focuses on Monitoring and Production Maintenance. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Runtime error logging
items.text: For Runtime error logging, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Frontend monitoring
items.text: For Frontend monitoring, decide which code runs during build, on the server, and in the browser. Keep output deterministic during hydration, isolate state per server request, keep secrets server-only, and test the actual production build rather than relying only on the dev server.

items.title: Performance monitoring
items.text: For Performance monitoring, measure first and optimize the constrained resource rather than guessing. Compare before/after behavior, keep stable identity for rendered lists, and verify that an optimization does not make the code harder to maintain.

items.title: Handling broken API dependencies
items.text: For Handling broken API dependencies, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Maintenance and dependency updates
items.text: For Maintenance and dependency updates, identify the reactive source that changes and the value or side effect that depends on it. Prefer computed values for derived data; use watchers when a change must trigger work outside pure derivation, and keep dependencies explicit.

content_blocks.code:
npm run build
npm run preview
content_blocks.expected_output: The built app is placed in dist/ and previewed locally. A successful preview still does not prove the hosting rewrite, headers, domain, or API environment is correct.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run from the project root; after deployment, test direct navigation to a nested route, refresh, HTTPS, environment settings, and API failure behavior.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Monitoring and Production Maintenance with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Frontend monitoring”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue rendering may be client-side, server-rendered, or pre-rendered; Nuxt provides an opinionated application framework for SSR/SSG use cases. For Monitoring and Production Maintenance, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Monitoring and Production Maintenance” that applies “Runtime error logging”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Runtime error logging”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Monitoring and Production Maintenance belongs to the broader area Server-Side Rendering, Nuxt, and Deployment.
The main concept to practice is Runtime error logging.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
